nodes.summary: For a group $G$, the bi-invariant orders of $G$ are the linear orders $\le$ on $G$ (reflexive, antisymmetric, transitive and total relations) that are invariant under left and right multiplication: for all $a, b, c \in G$, $a \le b$ implies $ca \le cb$ and $ac \le bc$.
nodes.title: Bi-invariant linear orders on a group

nodes.summary: There is a finitely presented group $G$ that admits a bi-invariant linear order and has a finite generating family $g_1, \dots, g_k$ for which the word problem is insoluble: no algorithm decides, given a word in the $g_i$ and their inverses, whether it equals $1$ in $G$.
nodes.title: Bludov–Glass: a finitely presented orderable group with insoluble word problem

nodes.title: Right orders of a group

nodes.summary: There exist a soluble group $G$ that admits a right order, a natural number $k$ and elements $g_0, \dots, g_{k-1}$ generating $G$ such that, for the homomorphism $\varphi$ from the free group on $k$ generators to $G$ sending the $i$-th generator to $g_i$, the group $G$ is recursively presented with respect to $\varphi$ and the word problem for $\varphi$ is not solvable.
